decisions.reason: Step 2.2 incorrectly excluded logical classical fan-out merely from port discipline. The repair first proves that every external classical record left undecoded by D is a transparent EC bypass: a last incident EC location could be faulted to reset its outgoing bit, contradicting D E_1 P_0=D P_0 on an encoded quantum input with that bit one. The same fixed-port argument excludes creating such a retained bit. Reroute these untouched wires directly from their original sources before forming the owner graph; recursive refinement preserves them since there is no EC location to replace on them. Decoded block records remain block bundles until measurement. All remaining external EC outputs are the successor block bundle, so the forward-path contraction argument applies without losing classical fan-out. The Statement and witness-tree counting are unchanged. AGP Sections 5.2.1–5.2.2 were consulted for expanded collars and syndrome-retaining bad operations; the bypass argument is supplied locally, not attributed to that source.

The full stabilizer syndrome has X-check part boundary(E) and zero Z-check part. Step 1.1 called the former the entire syndrome. Repaired that component statement explicitly; equality of X components still gives boundary(E triangle R)=0. The supplied path theorem proves a contained self-avoiding left-to-right crossing, and toggling it preserves relative boundary; minimality gives |R intersect P| <= |E intersect P| including ties. Statement unchanged; no consumer propagation.

The displayed fixed-recovery quantifier already requires correction without a supplied location set and permits different supports for different Kraus operators. Calling d located-error capacity was inconsistent terminology, not a missing recovery identity. Corrected it to unlocated-error capacity and made the support quantifier explicit. The distance condition 2d<d(S), encoded joint error-span recovery and stage contracts are unchanged. All six direct item consumers still use these same identities; source quote mirrors affected by the wording are recorded for owner maintenance.

The rejection overlooks the actual cited construction. Shor-correction Proof 1.2 explicitly synthesizes k-bit reversible truth tables with bound 2^k(8k+8); 1.3 constructs two cats, tripled Z1Zj checks and private per-coordinate enable workspaces; 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1 prove their fault cases; 9.1 counts their resources. Magic-state Proof 2.1 explicitly extends this finite procedure to 49 coordinates, supplies controlled-S and efficient selector logic, and 10.1 counts this extension separately. No missing cat or Boolean-circuit supplier is being assumed. The encoder, rank-one verification/fallback and injection proofs retain their stated error sectors and branch probabilities.

Fault-free at level zero has its ordinary meaning relative to the realized fault set, but this parameter was left implicit. Made F subset L(C) and the fixed q explicit, and defined level-zero badness by lambda in F. Finite recursion then defines a deterministic predicate of F restricted to the rectangle, so disjoint child indicators generate the bad events used by both probability bounds. The recursive threshold and disjointness condition are unchanged; direct consumers already work patternwise or probabilistically with this predicate.

Magic-state Proof 2.2 explicitly defines C0,C1 and f(z) as nearest-coset label, proves mutual distance nine and uniqueness through four bit errors. Its Proof 6.1 invokes Shor-correction Proof 1.2 to implement that same 49-input function reversibly, with private workspaces and per-coordinate controls. Thus initialization/readout F3 cites an actual previously constructed decoder, not an unsupported interface. The readout proof uses at most three changed bits with two incoming errors and one fault; each physical string selects a unique logical bra, retaining coherent branches and reference weights. No item edit is needed.

The former arbitrary upper-bound quantifier was false: eta=0 and p_r=1 for r>=1 are valid loose probability bounds but violate p_1<=A p_0^(q+1). Defined p_0=eta and p_{r+1}=min(1,A p_r^(q+1)), and proved these are uniform bounds. To preserve the Statement's one-sided badness rule, the proof bounds canonical local dominating events B_v, rather than assuming every possibly thinned bad event is local. These events have independent disjoint-child indicators; the union bound and induction prove the original closed form, including eta=0 and A=1. The direct threshold consumer uses only this unchanged numerical upper bound.

Magic-state Proof 1.1 explicitly constructs the bare encoder: complete x,b1,b2,b3 to a binary basis, apply H to three zero ancillas, synthesize the invertible binary linear map by CNOT/SWAP, then concatenate eight copies. This exactly realizes W on arbitrary logical inputs with no faults. Reversing that finite unitary circuit maps W psi back to psi tensor 48 zero coordinates. Thus this theorem's Steps 1.1 and 3.2 legitimately use both that encoder and its inverse, with Shor correction supplying code-valued output before the inverse. No fault tolerance is asserted for unknown-input bare encoding. Its stronger fixed weight-four recovery supplies the clarified unlocated capacity two; only the owning F6 contract quote requires synchronization.
